clue.text: Fact ultimately broadcast is politic

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so these letters are strewn into a new order

parts.note: ult. is the standard abbreviation of ultimately (ultimo)

explanation.surface: Spreading a fact at last is the sensible political move.
explanation.walkthrough: 'broadcast' scrambles FACT plus ULT, the abbreviation of 'ultimately'; the clue tempts you to take the last letter of 'Fact' instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Politic means shrewd and diplomatic, a close synonym of careful not to give offence.

clue.text: Fool at church showing evidence of nervousness

parts.note: a twit is a silly person, a fool

explanation.surface: A clown in church gives himself away by showing nerves.
explanation.definitionFit: A nervous tic or jerk of a muscle is a classic outward sign of anxiety.

clue.text: A pecan could be served with the drinks

definitions.text: A pecan could be served with the drinks

indicators.note: the letters are dished up in a different arrangement, as food is plated anew

explanation.surface: A nut might be offered as a snack alongside the drinks.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is the definition as well as the wordplay: rearranging A PECAN gives an item that a nut-topped titbit might well be.
explanation.definitionFit: A small savoury titbit on bread or pastry is the classic thing handed round with drinks.

clue.text: Mail given priority, showing best form

definitions.meaning: the faster, dearer tier of the British postal service

explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names both the premium British post class and anything of top quality.

clue.text: Student able to change designation

parts.note: L is a learner, from the plate on a learner driver's car

indicators.note: the letters of the word able are told to alter into a new order

explanation.surface: A student can get his title altered.
explanation.definitionFit: A label is a name or tag given to something, a designation.

clue.text: Traffic controller's lines set in committee

indicators.note: one piece is placed inside the other, as a jewel is set in a ring

parts.note: a board is a governing committee
L is an abbreviation for line, doubled for the plural

explanation.surface: The traffic warden's guidelines are being fixed by a committee.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'controller's' stands for 'is', a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A short post in the road that keeps vehicles out of an area acts as a traffic controller.

clue.text: Game of little importance

definitions.meaning: a table game with balls struck into holes, a kind of bar billiards

explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a table game played with balls and pins and a mere trifle.

clue.text: Set down face up

indicators.note: in a down clue the word is read from the bottom upwards, reversing it

parts.note: the dial is the face of a clock or watch

explanation.surface: Put something down with its face upwards.
explanation.walkthrough: 'face up' looks like part of the instruction for placing a card, but 'face' is DIAL and 'up' turns it round in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Laid is the past tense of lay, meaning put or set something down.

clue.text: Expresses approval for application by young men to go round university

parts.note: an app is a software application

indicators.note: the young men surround the following letter, enclosing it

parts.note: lads are young men

explanation.surface: Someone praises a request from young men to tour a campus.
explanation.definitionFit: To clap or cheer someone is to express approval of them.

clue.text: Rory's idea mostly out of order — ridiculous!

indicators.note: letters that are out of order must be put back into a fresh sequence

parts.note: the name taken with its S as letters

indicators.note: most of the word idea is used, dropping its final letter

explanation.surface: Rory's notion is hopelessly wrong and quite absurd.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mostly' trims idea to IDE, which joins RORYS before the jumble.
explanation.definitionFit: Derisory means so small or inadequate as to be laughable, ridiculous.

clue.text: The meal's not the first provided by the "Bull"

indicators.note: the opening letter of the meal word is dropped

parts.note: dinner is a meal; the 's stands for is

explanation.surface: The main course comes courtesy of the Bull, a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The Bull' reads as a pub name, but it is the target's centre in darts or archery.
explanation.definitionFit: On a target the inner ring lies right next to the centre, and the inner bull is the bullseye itself.

clue.text: "Fair" could include me; I'm very much up and down

definitions.text: "Fair" could include me; I'm very much up and down

parts.words: "Fair" could include me; I'm very much up and down
parts.note: a funfair ride that climbs and plunges, speaking of itself

explanation.definitionFit: A roller coaster at a funfair constantly rises and falls steeply.

clue.text: Yield a title and a cup when beaten

indicators.note: beaten as eggs are beaten, so the letters are mixed up

explanation.surface: A losing side concedes both the title and the trophy.
explanation.definitionFit: To capitulate is to surrender, to yield to an opponent.

clue.text: Criticises card game's return

indicators.note: the card game's name comes back the other way, read in reverse

parts.note: snap is a children's card game

explanation.surface: Someone attacks a card game's revival.
explanation.definitionFit: To pan a play or film is to criticise it harshly.

clue.text: Fix heap etc, moving to lead the way

parts.note: to set is to fix in place

indicators.note: the letters are moved about into a new order

explanation.surface: Instructions to sort out a pile of odds and ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To set the pace is to lead, determining the speed others must follow.

clue.text: Acceptable amount of cash

parts.note: money that must lawfully be accepted in payment of a debt

explanation.definitionFit: Notes and coins which by law must be accepted when offered in payment are legally acceptable cash.

clue.text: It good finding out about making a complaint

parts.note: to rumble someone is to find them out, see through them

explanation.surface: Discovering things is good for having a moan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It' at the start gives no letters and acts only as a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Grumbling is complaining in a low, discontented way.

clue.text: Items sprayed with it are moist, mostly

definitions.text: Items sprayed with it are moist, mostly

indicators.note: the letters are sent out in a spray, so they land in a new order

explanation.surface: Things treated by this device end up mostly damp.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines a spray device, and ARE MOIST rearranged spells it; 'mostly' only completes the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A device that turns liquid into a fine spray leaves whatever it hits damp.

clue.text: CIA lab is built in assembly room

indicators.note: the letters are constructed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: An intelligence laboratory is constructed inside a meeting hall.
explanation.definitionFit: A basilica was originally a Roman hall of assembly, later a church of that form.

clue.text: We, returning from Newcastle, turn off — clear?

indicators.note: the letters go off course, scrambled into a new order
the reversed pair is taken away from the city's name
the word we is read backwards

explanation.surface: Driving back from a northern city, we take the exit, if it's clear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'returning' gives EW, which 'from' removes from NEWCASTLE leaving NCASTLE; 'off' jumbles that with TURN. Newcastle is a city in north-east England.
explanation.definitionFit: Translucent means letting light through, in a loose sense clear.

clue.text: Brief sleep at work? No lying!

definitions.text: Brief sleep at work? No lying!

parts.words: Brief sleep at work? No lying!
parts.note: a short doze snatched at the desk, sitting up rather than lying down

explanation.definitionFit: A short light sleep, typically taken in a chair rather than in bed.

clue.text: Woman in credit with a selection of wine

indicators.note: the woman goes inside the credit abbreviation

parts.note: CR is the accounting abbreviation for credit
Ella is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman in the black buys some wine.
explanation.definitionFit: A cellar is a stock of wine kept by a person or restaurant.

clue.text: Island, including island in the sea

indicators.note: the first island takes the second inside it

parts.note: the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea
the Isle of Man, an island in the Irish Sea

explanation.surface: One island holds another in the middle of the ocean.
explanation.definitionFit: The main is a poetic and old term for the open sea.

clue.text: Lob with spin to go over the same ground and cause destruction

indicators.note: a ball with spin twists, so the letters are turned about

parts.words: to go over the same ground
parts.note: to iterate is to repeat, going over it again

explanation.surface: A tennis lob with topspin covers the court again and wrecks the opponent.
explanation.definitionFit: To obliterate is to destroy utterly, wiping something out.

clue.text: Metrical stress is cut out

indicators.note: the letters are put out of their order

explanation.surface: The emphasis in a verse line is removed.
explanation.definitionFit: In prosody an ictus is the beat or accent that falls on a stressed syllable.

clue.text: Bird (not strong) found on Scottish island

indicators.note: the letter for forte, meaning strong in music, is removed

parts.note: a finch is a small songbird

explanation.surface: A small bird turns up on an island off Scotland.
explanation.walkthrough: F is forte, loud or strong in music. Inch is a Scottish word for a small island.
explanation.definitionFit: Inch, from Gaelic innis, is a word for a small island in Scotland.

clue.text: A natural student?

parts.note: someone who studies the natural sciences, not one born to study

explanation.definitionFit: A natural scientist studies the natural world, and the clue drops the first word.

clue.text: Cancel yearbook that's missing one

indicators.note: a letter standing for one, A, is lost from the yearbook word

parts.note: an annual is a book published once a year

explanation.surface: Scrap the yearbook since one copy is lost.
explanation.definitionFit: To annul a marriage or contract is to declare it void, cancelling it.

clue.text: He's no pig, but he won't let others pass

definitions.text: He's no pig, but he won't let others pass

parts.words: He's no pig, but he won't let others pass
parts.note: a selfish driver hogging the road, compared to a greedy swine

explanation.definitionFit: An inconsiderate motorist who blocks other vehicles from overtaking.

clue.text: A dozy supporter?

parts.note: a beam under railway rails that also sounds like someone asleep

explanation.definitionFit: A railway sleeper supports the rails, and the word also means a person sleeping.
